representations.text: Over 28 baseline days, sleep averaged 470 min (start ~22:50, end fixed 07:00), steps ~8054, activity ~55 min, RHR 56 bpm, RMSSD 44.5 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep, steps, activity, low movement, and RHR remained near baseline. RMSSD dropped to a mean of 39.4 ms with high variance (22–47 ms) from Apr 3–6 before recovering to 43–47 ms by Apr 7. Daytime activity occurred consistently around 21:00; daytime low-movement blocks spanned ~10:00–18:00. No strong cross-metric relationships were observed.

During the 28-day baseline, sleep averaged 470 min starting ~22:50 and ending exactly 07:00 daily, steps ~7940, activity ~54 min, RHR 55.8 bpm, RMSSD 44.2 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep timing shifted markedly: starts alternated between ~22:15 and ~00:40, ends between 06:30 and 09:00, increasing mean sleep to 478 min (+8.5). Steps rose slightly to ~8052. Activity, low movement, RHR (~56.4), and RMSSD (~45.0) stayed near baseline. The prior rigid schedule became variable; no strong metric correlations emerged.

Across 28 baseline days, sleep averaged 471 min (start ~22:50, end fixed 07:00), steps ~7947, activity ~56 min, RHR 55.9 bpm, RMSSD 45.0 ms. In the 14-day window, activity alternated strictly between 90 and 45 min (mean 64.3 vs 55.6 baseline). Sleep split into two phases: days 1–6 maintained ~479 min, then days 7–14 abruptly shortened to ~385–392 min with starts shifting to ~00:08–00:15 and reduced nighttime coverage (~405–412 min vs ~490 baseline). Steps (~8088), RHR, and RMSSD remained stable throughout.

During the 28-day baseline, sleep averaged 465 min (start ~22:55, end fixed 07:00), steps ~7983, activity ~56 min, RHR 56.1 bpm, RMSSD 44.8 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep onset delayed sharply to ~00:47–01:05 with duration falling to a mean of 346 min (−118 min, range 335–355). Nighttime coverage dropped to 355–373 min from ~486 baseline. Steps (~8037), activity (~55 min), low movement, RHR (55.4 bpm), and RMSSD (44.9 ms) remained near baseline levels throughout.
